name: meta-tagging platform - concept definition component
note: Every score in this product is recomputed in the browser from verdicts.json and cases.json. Nothing is precomputed except the verdicts themselves. An agent given only these files can reproduce every published number; that is the acceptance test for machine accessibility, and it is checked at build time by TOOLS/build_platform_data.py.
license: CC BY 4.0 for the tag layer. Paper text is (c) its authors and is linked, never redistributed here; quotes are short and for identification.

papers.json.what: one record per paper a visitor can put in a corpus

cases.json.what: one record per case; `quote` is an exact substring of the paper

fields.status: 'P' asserted art | 'N' asserted not art | 'U' the literature does not decide

definitions.json.what: the rival definitions, their gate verdict and their published score

fields.proposed_by: string|null - the person who proposed it
fields.proposed_on: string|null - ISO date. With proposed_by this is a dated public record of priority, which is the only thing that protects a one-sentence definition; copyright does not reach it.
fields.cited: string|null - the published work the position comes from, for the definitions drawn from the literature.
fields.theorist: string|null - the name as tagged in papers.json, so a reader can restrict the corpus to the papers that discuss this theorist and re-score there.
fields.wording: 'ours'|null - 'ours' means the sentence on screen is OUR one-line summary of the position, not a quotation. Every literature definition here is 'ours'. The cases are verbatim; the definitions are not, and the two must never be read as if they were held to the same standard.
fields.n_papers_on_theorist: number - how many corpus papers carry that theorist tag.

criteria.json.what: 14 candidate criteria for defining art, OFFERED and not imposed. The interface lets a reader keep, drop or add to them and composes the wording. They are NOT scored: scoring means judging every case in the same run as the definitions, and a score from a separate run is not comparable with the numbers here.

fields.excludes_en: string - what the criterion rules out
fields.excludes_he: string - our translation, not source text

concepts.json.what: the registry the concept picker searches: every concept the tool knows about and what state it is in. Two have a scored definition board; the rest are terms the main corpus discusses but for which no board has been built, and the interface says so rather than pretending. Not art-specific - it spans the whole site - but it lives here because data/ is the root the pages resolve against.

fields.dir: string - where a ready concept's files are, relative to data/
fields.calib: string - the control that must score near +1.000 for that concept. It is NOT the same control for every concept.

cases.jsonl.what: cases.json as JSON Lines - one self-contained JSON object per line. Same content, same build, no separate endpoint. Offered because a streaming reader, a grep and a truncated download all work on it.

verdicts.json.what: definition id -> one character per case, in case index order

how_to_score: Pick a set of paper ids. Take every case whose paper is in the set and whose status is P or N. SKIP any case whose verdict character is '-': it was never judged, and counting it as a rejection is the single easiest way to get every number on this site wrong (it yields circular 0.608 instead of 0.983). Of the cases that remain, compare the verdict character to the status ('1' vs 'P' = true positive). Then MCC = (TP*TN - FP*FN) / sqrt((TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN)). The 'circular' definition must score near +1.000 on any corpus; if it does not, the coding contradicts itself and no other number in that view may be read.

canonical_corpus.note: Two counts are true at once and the difference matters: papers_total is what has been tagged, papers_scored is what carries verdicts and can be scored. Papers with n_scored == 0 are tagged but not yet judged, and the interface will not let them be selected. Every published score in definitions.json is over cases_adjudicated.

field_notes.papers.n_scored: how many of this paper's cases carry verdicts. 0 means tagged but not scored; such a paper contributes nothing to any metric and cannot be selected in the interface.
field_notes.papers.words: word count of the stored full text; provenance only.
field_notes.papers.has_senses: whether a sense record exists for this paper.
field_notes.papers.url: null means we hold no retrievable link for this paper. Seven of the scored papers are in this state - the pre-2010 classics - and they contribute 98 of the 355 adjudicated cases. Their quotes were verified against stored text, but a third party cannot re-check them from this site alone. Said plainly because it is a real limit on verifiability, not a formatting gap.
field_notes.definitions.published.lo/hi: 95% confidence interval from a PAPER-CLUSTERED bootstrap - papers are resampled with replacement, not cases, because cases from one paper are one author's usage and are not independent. 2000 resamples, percentile interval. A case-level bootstrap does NOT reproduce these numbers and should not be expected to.
field_notes.definitions.provenance: who proposed this definition. 'literature' = attested in a published paper; 'user' = proposed by a reader of this tool and tested here, which is allowed because definitions are hypotheses under test and only the CASES must come from the literature; 'user+tool' = a user definition with a wording change the measurement proposed; 'control' = deliberately bad, present to calibrate.
field_notes.definitions.published.circularity_distan: the fraction of adjudicated cases on which this definition returns the same verdict as the circular control. High is not good: it means the definition reproduces the consensus rather than explaining it.

calibration_rule.on_failure: the coding contradicts itself for that corpus; no other number from it may be read. The interface raises this warning itself.
calibration_rule.undefined_mcc: when a corpus yields no negative cases (or no positives) the MCC denominator is zero and the score is undefined, not zero. Such rows are dropped rather than shown as 0.000.

reference_scorer: reference_scorer.py - a short, dependency-free implementation that reproduces every published score from these files. Run it to check your own reading before trusting it.
limitations: Single coder: the cases were coded in one pass, so two-independent-coder reliability is not met and is not claimed.
Scores are comparable only WITHIN one run. Instruction wording alone moves MCC by about 0.12 for an identical definition.
Confidence intervals overlap heavily at the top; ranks are not separable.
The corpus tilts contemporary. That was a deliberate choice and it affects every number here.
